# Second Brain review

Use this before a handoff or during a weekly review for a selected project in an installed Second Brain workspace.

The canonical procedure is `03-Resources/Procedures/review.md`. It is owned by the installed template, not by this skill.

1. Read the selected project's facts, roadmap, decisions, and newest three progress entries.
2. Compare every `Done` claim with its roadmap item and required evidence.
3. Record and repair a conflict when progress says complete while the roadmap remains `Open`; do not report ready while evidence is missing.
4. Put confirmed rules in the appropriate project or global decisions record, then end with one `Next` action.
5. Use the installed learning procedure only when a correction is worth keeping.

# Manual context route

Use this only for the selected project folder. Do not scan the broader vault, parent folders, secrets, unrelated projects, or private notes.

Shared instructions belong in `AGENTS.md`; `CLAUDE.md` imports that owner. For navigation, choose the relevant [operating](README.md), [project](../01-Projects/README.md), or [resource](../03-Resources/README.md) map and follow its owner links only when needed. Maps do not replace the prerequisite order below.

Read in this order when the files exist:

1. `00-Meta/Decisions.md`
2. The selected project's own `AGENTS.md`, `RULES.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, relevant `ai_rules/`, memory bank, and `README.md` before diagnosing or changing its files
3. `01-Projects/Selected-Project/FACTS.md`
4. `01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md`
5. `01-Projects/Selected-Project/Decisions.md`
6. The three newest entries in `01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md`
7. `00-Meta/Daily-Task-Plan.md` only if today's focus changes the task

`Selected-Project` stands for your project folder. A new project is a copy of `03-Resources/_templates/project/`; the [project map](../01-Projects/README.md) owns that rule.

Then state: selected root, selected project, files read, current goal, constraints, next useful action, evidence required for done, and any conflict. If a completed progress entry conflicts with an open roadmap item, name the conflict. Do not call the project ready.

Capture new work with `03-Resources/Procedures/capture.md`. Never invent a fact, decision, or verification result.

For system architecture changes to rules, commands, skills, workflows, automations, handoffs or context routing, use `second-brain-icm` before editing. If native skill invocation is unavailable, manually read `.agents/skills/second-brain-icm/SKILL.md` or `.claude/skills/second-brain-icm/SKILL.md`, then the method it names, `icm-architect/SKILL.md` in the same skills folder. # Close

Open the roadmap item and its progress entries together.

1. Record what was Done in `progress.md`.
2. Add the exact evidence under Verified. A completed action without evidence stays Open or In progress.
3. Update the roadmap status to `Verified` only when the evidence listed there was checked.
4. Write any remaining work as Open and name the Next action.

Use these words plainly: Done, Verified, Open, Next. They make handoffs readable and expose wishful completion.

# Review

Run this weekly or before a handoff.

1. Read facts, roadmap, decisions, and the newest three progress entries.
2. Compare each `Done` claim with its roadmap item and required evidence.
3. If progress says complete while the roadmap is Open, record a conflict. Repair the record or collect the missing evidence. Do not report ready.
4. Promote a confirmed rule to the project's `Decisions.md`, or to `00-Meta/Decisions.md` only when it affects multiple projects.
5. Check the [keeping-it-clean rules](../../00-Meta/README.md#keeping-it-clean) and fix any file that breaks one.
6. End with one `Next` action.

Use [learning and scaling](learning-and-scaling.md) when a correction is worth keeping.

## Inputs

- Working (this run): the selected project's [roadmap](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md) and the newest three entries in [progress](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md).
- Reference (every run): the selected project's [facts](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/FACTS.md) and [decisions](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/Decisions.md).

## Outputs

- Any repaired row in `01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md` or conflict noted in `01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md`.
- A confirmed rule in the project's `Decisions.md`, or in `00-Meta/Decisions.md` when it affects several projects.
- One `Next` action.

## Human check

Read the `Next` action and each conflict the review found. Confirm that no item reads ready while its evidence is missing.

Each task is one line: a checkbox, a priority from P0 to P4, then the task. Tools may read these lines, so keep the shape. The rules are in [keeping it clean](README.md#keeping-it-clean).

## Open decisions or blockers

- Done: [what changed]
- Verified: [evidence and where it lives]
- Open: [what remains]

# Home

## Start my first result

> Read Home and First use. Help me agree one small saved result, ask only what is missing, and show the exact plan before edits.

Follow [First use](03-Resources/Procedures/first-use.md). Undecided? Try learning one idea from a paragraph you supply.

## Continue my project

> Read Home and Context. Recover my saved Next action and its evidence, then help me continue without repeating setup.

Follow [Context](03-Resources/Procedures/context.md), then [Close](03-Resources/Procedures/close.md) to save what changed and the next step.

## Connect a repository

A repository you already work in can be registered here. From the starter copy, run `node ./bin/second-brain.mjs connect --target <this folder> --repo <that repository>`. It prints the complete plan and writes nothing until you approve that exact digest.

On a repository with no Spec Harness files (the harness is the set of agent rules and commands that Spec Harness installs), approval stages them there. The files are uncommitted, and your team decides whether they go in by pull request. Then open the repository in your client and run `/sdd init`. The repository stays STAGED until `.claude/agents/.init-synthesis.json` exists.

Each connection gets a folder under `01-Projects/` with its own `README.md` and a `Connection.md` record. Run `node ./bin/second-brain.mjs verify --target <this folder>` from the starter copy to see each connection's current status.

These four link to `Selected-Project`, the seeded project. For another project, use the same four records in its folder under `01-Projects/`.

[Facts](01-Projects/Selected-Project/FACTS.md) · [Roadmap](01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md) · [Progress](01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md) · [Decisions](01-Projects/Selected-Project/Decisions.md)

Current values live in these owners. Home only points to them. Any other project keeps its records in its own folder under `01-Projects/`, a copy of the project template, with its own `README.md` map. Its code stays where it is.

## When a need repeats

[Your extensions](03-Resources/Extensions.md) links your reusable references and methods. Use [Extend](03-Resources/Procedures/extend.md) for a named repeated need after first use.

## More

- Daily work: [Focus](00-Meta/Daily-Task-Plan.md), [Capture](03-Resources/Procedures/capture.md), [Review](03-Resources/Procedures/review.md).

Before working, name one project folder and read the route in [00-Meta/AGENTS.md](../../00-Meta/AGENTS.md).

Return this compact note:

- Goal: [from facts]
- Constraints: [from facts and decisions]

Read the installed Home, the operating route above, and the selected project map. Load only the records that route lists, at the depth it states. Recover the goal, constraints, actual artifact path and check evidence, Open work and saved Next action into the compact note above. Open the artifact to confirm the claimed evidence; name any mismatch as Conflict before proceeding. Ask only for information still missing from these owners.

Use a genuinely separate new chat with only the installed target and this manual owner route. A same-chat reread does not establish recovery. Native automatic loading remains unverified until observed in the client.

# First use

Use after verified installation in one confirmed target. This is the owner for personalization, one useful result and continuation. Setup belongs to the source ONBOARDING contract; Home and maps only navigate.

## 1. Recover the current state

Read the installed root `AGENTS.md`, then follow [Context](context.md) and its required [manual route](../../00-Meta/AGENTS.md). Read only those scoped owners and the installation receipt/current state when resuming setup. Stop on contradictions or failed verification. Client and operating-system permissions still apply; these instructions do not grant access.

Reuse answers and evidence already available in this selected target or chat. Preserve personalized records and existing history. Repeated or interrupted setup fills only actual gaps; do not replay completed edits. For returning use, recover the saved Next action through Context and continue that work without asking setup questions whose answers already exist.

## 2. Only ask what is missing

Ask only missing goal, current work, desired output and constraints. Use these prompts only for unanswered parts:

- What would you like to learn or finish, and what work have you already started?
- What small saved result would be useful at the end of this session?
- What limits should we respect, such as time, available material or tools? Mark unknowns unknown; never invent a deadline, fact, decision or verification result.

If the user is undecided, offer the existing learn-one-idea example below: ask for a paragraph they want to understand and obtain their confirmation of its goal and output before continuing. Suggest the saved learning note and paragraph comparison; do not choose or write automatically. A project can be learning or planning; coding is optional.

## 2a. Profile: only what is missing

Read `00-Meta/Profile.md` first. Ask only what is still `Unknown`. `init.md` owns the questions for Role, How I want answers and Never touch. `complete-init.md` owns the question for Stack (section 1, question 1). Ask each still-`Unknown` field with its owner's exact question, and do not write a new question for a Profile field.

Record anything the person cannot or will not answer as `Unknown` and list it under `## Unknown`. Do not invent a role, stack, preference or boundary. Write `00-Meta/Profile.md` under the same exact-plan approval and preimage rule as the next section. The read order in `00-Meta/AGENTS.md` puts Profile first, so read the `Never touch` entries before changing anything. Do not assume the client loads it automatically.

Do not record credentials, tokens, client names or anything confidential. `Never touch` names paths and areas, not secrets.

## 3. Approve the exact personalization

Show the exact personalized-record plan: file paths, proposed edits, evidence/source and unknowns. Use the existing [Facts](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/FACTS.md), [Roadmap](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md), [Decisions](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/Decisions.md), [Progress](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md) and [Daily task plan](../../00-Meta/Daily-Task-Plan.md) as state owners, only when their actual gaps require edits.

Obtain approval for that exact plan before edits. Preserve exact preimages and check current bytes for concurrent edits; stop on conflict. Append history rather than replacing it. Check approved edits against the plan. Existing personalized values stay intact unless the user explicitly approves a change.

The installer receipt rollback covers only its transaction. It does not automatically undo later personalization or artifacts. Keep their separate preimages and agree recovery before editing user-owned work.

## 4. Agree one useful artifact

Agree one small artifact, its exact file, scope and falsifiable check. Obtain approval for that artifact plan before producing it. Read the selected project's rules before touching its files. Use [Capture](capture.md) to record the outcome, owner, evidence required and next action in the roadmap.

Produce the approved artifact, run the agreed check and keep observable evidence. An offered task, blank template or promised result is not completed work. A failed check leaves the outcome Open or In progress.

## Noncoding example: learn one idea

This is an example to adapt with the user, not evidence of completed work.

- Goal: understand one idea from a user-provided paragraph in 15 minutes.
- Artifact: `01-Projects/Selected-Project/learning-note.md`, with the idea in plain language, one example and one next action.
- Scope: only the supplied paragraph; unsupported details stay unknown.
- Check: compare the note with that paragraph, identify the supporting sentence for each claim and confirm an actionable next step. Record the actual check result.
- PARA: the note belongs in Projects because this learning outcome has a finish line; reusable reference belongs in Resources and inactive work in Archives.
- CODE: Capture the paragraph and task; Organize them with this project; Distill the idea and example; Express them as the checked note and next action.

Follow the same personalization and artifact approvals above. See [PARA + CODE](../PARA-CODE.md) for definitions.

## 5. Close with evidence

Follow [Close](close.md). Record Done, Verified, Open and Next in existing progress, and reconcile the roadmap with actual evidence. Done means produced; Verified means the agreed check passed. Keep unresolved work visible. Show the artifact path and check result to the user.

## 6. Continue in a NEW chat

Start a new chat in the installed target. Read root `AGENTS.md` manually if the client has not confirmed loading it, then read `00-Meta/AGENTS.md` and the owners required by [Context](context.md). Recover the goal, constraints, output evidence and Next from those files, not the previous chat's memory. Name any contradiction and stop a success claim until it is resolved.

A same-chat reread is rehearsal. A synthetic walkthrough is fixture evidence. Fresh-client acceptance and authenticated discovery remain unverified until separately observed.

# PARA and CODE

Tiago Forte created both PARA and CODE. They solve different parts of the same problem.

## PARA: where a record belongs

- Projects: active work with a finish line.
- Areas: ongoing responsibilities.
- Resources: reference material and procedures.
- Archives: inactive material kept for retrieval.

This starter also keeps `00-Meta` for operating rules and `05-Daily` for short-lived daily state. Those folders are additions, not replacements for PARA.

## CODE: how work moves

- Capture: record an input before it disappears.
- Organise: put it with the project, area, resource, or archive that owns it.
- Distil: keep the next useful fact, decision, or procedure easy to find.
- Express: use the material to finish and verify an outcome.

PARA gives the file a home. CODE gives the work a direction. A captured task becomes useful when its roadmap row names an owner, evidence, and next action.

# Learning and scaling

Learning is a recorded correction, not a claim that an AI silently improved itself.

1. Capture one confirmed miss and its cause.
2. Put the rule where it belongs: facts for changing values, decisions for choices, procedures for repeatable work.
3. In a fresh session, ask for the rule before work begins.
4. Mark it verified only when that session follows it.

As the vault grows, keep one owner per fact, archive finished projects, and load procedures only when the task needs them. Add automation after the manual path works and you can explain its failure mode.

## 1. Recover the current state

Read the installed root `AGENTS.md`, then follow [Context](context.md) and its required [manual route](../../00-Meta/AGENTS.md). Read only those scoped owners and the installation receipt/current state when resuming setup. Stop on contradictions or failed verification. Client and operating-system permissions still apply; these instructions do not grant access.

Reuse answers and evidence already available in this selected target or chat. Preserve personalized records and existing history. Repeated or interrupted setup fills only actual gaps; do not replay completed edits. For returning use, recover the saved Next action through Context and continue that work without asking setup questions whose answers already exist.

## 2. Only ask what is missing

Ask only missing goal, current work, desired output and constraints. Use these prompts only for unanswered parts:

- What would you like to learn or finish, and what work have you already started?
- What small saved result would be useful at the end of this session?
- What limits should we respect, such as time, available material or tools? Mark unknowns unknown; never invent a deadline, fact, decision or verification result.

If the user is undecided, offer the existing learn-one-idea example below: ask for a paragraph they want to understand and obtain their confirmation of its goal and output before continuing. Suggest the saved learning note and paragraph comparison; do not choose or write automatically. A project can be learning or planning; coding is optional.

## 3. Approve the exact personalization

Show the exact personalized-record plan: file paths, proposed edits, evidence/source and unknowns. Use the existing [Facts](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/FACTS.md), [Roadmap](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md), [Decisions](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/Decisions.md), [Progress](../../01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md) and [Daily task plan](../../00-Meta/Daily-Task-Plan.md) as state owners, only when their actual gaps require edits.

Obtain approval for that exact plan before edits. Preserve exact preimages and check current bytes for concurrent edits; stop on conflict. Append history rather than replacing it. Check approved edits against the plan. Existing personalized values stay intact unless the user explicitly approves a change.

The installer receipt rollback covers only its transaction. It does not automatically undo later personalization or artifacts. Keep their separate preimages and agree recovery before editing user-owned work.

## 4. Agree one useful artifact

Agree one small artifact, its exact file, scope and falsifiable check. Obtain approval for that artifact plan before producing it. Read the selected project's rules before touching its files. Use [Capture](capture.md) to record the outcome, owner, evidence required and next action in the roadmap.

2. The selected project's own `AGENTS.md`, `RULES.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, relevant `ai_rules/`, memory bank, and `README.md` before diagnosing or changing its files
3. `01-Projects/Selected-Project/FACTS.md`
4. `01-Projects/Selected-Project/roadmap.md`
5. `01-Projects/Selected-Project/Decisions.md`
6. The three newest entries in `01-Projects/Selected-Project/progress.md`
7. `00-Meta/Daily-Task-Plan.md` only if today's focus changes the task

`Selected-Project` is the seeded project and stands for the project you are working in: for another project, read the same four records in its folder under `01-Projects/`. Its code stays where it is. This route never scans for repositories; the person names each one. A new project is a copy of `03-Resources/_templates/project/`; the [project map](../01-Projects/README.md) owns that rule.

A repository registered with `connect` is another project. Its folder under `01-Projects/` has a `Connection.md` that records the repository path, the remote if one was readable, the rule files found and the status at connect time. That status is a record, not a live reading: `verify` re-checks it. Read the repository's own rules and memory in the repository before changing its files.

Then state: selected root, selected project, files read, current goal, constraints, next useful action, evidence required for done, and any conflict. If a completed progress entry conflicts with an open roadmap item, name the conflict. Do not call the project ready.

Capture new work with `03-Resources/Procedures/capture.md`. Never invent a fact, decision, or verification result.

For system architecture changes to rules, commands, skills, workflows, automations, handoffs or context routing, use `second-brain-icm` before editing. If native skill invocation is unavailable, manually read `.agents/skills/second-brain-icm/SKILL.md` or `.claude/skills/second-brain-icm/SKILL.md`, then the method it names, `icm-architect/SKILL.md` in the same skills folder. Ordinary note work uses the selected-project route above without loading architecture safeguards.
